### Added
- `make verify-all`: every `verify-*` target of `Makefile.custom.mk` in one target, which is what CI runs. The list is read out of that file, so a new `verify-*` target reaches CI by existing and nothing names the set twice; `make help` lists what each one asserts. The `test-ingress-modes` job named all 37 of them on one line, which drifted from the Makefile on every addition.
- `make e2e KUBECONFIG=… [SCENARIO=…] [CLUSTER_TYPE=…] [VALUES=…]`: runs one ATS scenario against any cluster. It packages the chart and hands the suite its inputs. `SCENARIO` is the pytest marker (`smoke` or `functional`), `CLUSTER_TYPE` picks the scenario defaults (`kind` or `eks`), and `VALUES` replaces the scenario's values-file list. `E2E_DOMAIN`, `E2E_ISSUER_URL`, `E2E_CLIENT_ID` and `E2E_IDP_SECRET_NAME` (the name of a Secret already on the cluster, not a credential) become a temporary values overlay layered last and removed on exit; `tests/e2e_overlay.py` renders it, and the target prints its line count, never a value. Each of those names one fact the chart and the tests both need, so the target derives the suite's `ATS_ISSUER_URL`, `ATS_CLIENT_ID`, `ATS_IDP_CA_SECRET` and — on a cluster type other than `kind` — `ATS_MUSTER_BASE_URL` from them, and an `ATS_` variable already in the environment wins. A `KUBECONFIG` with a leading `~` is expanded, which zsh does not do for an argument of that form. Documented in `tests/ats/README.md`.
- `helm/agent-platform/examples/kind-lab-dex.yaml`: the kind lab shape as a shipped example, moved from `tests/test-values.yaml` with its values unchanged (its header comment carries the install recipe and the no-secret statement). It is the file the ATS smoke installs, and `test_the_scenario_installs_the_example_file` asserts the scenario names an example file the repository ships. `.ats/main.yaml` and `make verify-self`'s lab-shape render follow the new path.
### Changed
- The ATS suite takes its cluster-specific inputs from a `Scenario` (`tests/ats/scenarios.py`, one per cluster shape) instead of kind literals, so the same assertions run on any cluster. Five groups become fields, each with its own environment variable: the values files (`ATS_VALUES`, plus `ATS_OVERLAY_VALUES` layered last), the identity provider (`ATS_ISSUER_URL`, `ATS_CLIENT_ID`, `ATS_CLIENT_SECRET`, `ATS_REGISTRATION_TOKEN`, `ATS_IDP_USER`, `ATS_IDP_PASSWORD`, `ATS_IDP_CA_SECRET`), the OAuth redirect (`ATS_OAUTH_CALLBACK`), muster's base URL and how it is reached (`ATS_MUSTER_BASE_URL`, `ATS_MUSTER_REACH`) and the budgets (`ATS_INSTALL_TIMEOUT`, `ATS_UNINSTALL_TIMEOUT`, `ATS_UNINSTALL_BUDGET_S`, `ATS_READY_TIMEOUT_S`). A port is read out of the URL that carries it, so the two can never disagree. `ATS_CLUSTER_TYPE` gains `eks`, whose scenario installs no lab Dex, port-forwards nothing and carries no default issuer, client, base URL or values file. An unknown cluster type, an unknown reach, a budget that is not an integer, a missing issuer, client or base URL, a values file that does not exist, and a non-kind scenario without `ATS_VALUES`, each fail the run with a message naming the variable. `make verify-scenarios` asserts the loader and the `make e2e` overlay offline. Every field defaults to the value it had, so `ATS_CLUSTER_TYPE=kind` with nothing else set installs the same three values files with the same ports, budgets and credentials.
